correctness.rationale: The edgewise equation u_v b_w=u_w b_v is exactly equivalent to simultaneous centralization because edge-center coordinates are independent. Outside the nonzero support, undominated vertices contribute one each. Each induced support component has exactly one free scalar if all coefficient t-vectors are proportional and none otherwise: a nonproportional edge kills both scalars and zero propagates through the connected component. Counting constant and nonconstant projective lines produces P and P^k-P, with independent (q-1) factors and q^(tm) central lifts. Normalization at T=1 yields q^(t(n+m)); sharp maxima n-c(G) and n-i(G) are proved and attained. The extracted checker independently verifies 132 cases/400389 vertex tuples over F2,F3,F4 and all 64 four-vertex graphs at t=2,q=2. This is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem determines a complete natural stabilizer-rank invariant for all finite graphical class-two Lie algebras, over every field and for every arity. Via orbit-stabilizer it gives all simultaneous-conjugation orbit sizes, rather than only a commuting probability or one-element count. The intrinsic center-cutting threshold is exactly two when the graph has an edge; max rank jumps from n-c(G) to n-i(G). The top coefficient encodes projectively nonconstant induced dominating components. Binary path and star with equal vertex/edge counts have substantially different full spectra, demonstrating structural information.
